comments.body:
## Independent root-cause corroboration, and confirmation the fix works

This bug resurfaced from a different direction: `make verify` on an unrelated change (604c-ade8, which touches only `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py`) came back with 18 failures where 17 were the known macOS-arm64 pandoc family. The 18th was `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py::test_file_impact_close_fetches_before_rejecting_stale_clone`, failing deterministically in isolation under `-p no:randomly`.

It reproduced in a second worktree whose only diff from `origin/main` was unrelated test infrastructure, which rules out both changes as the cause and confirms it is live on `origin/main` today.

A root-cause pass done without reference to this ticket landed on exactly the mechanism recorded here, which is worth capturing because it was derived independently:

- `_check_work_landed()` at `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:190-214` does refresh remotes and does call `_referencing_commits(..., include_upstream=True)`. The fetch is not the defect.
- `commit_impact.referencing_commits()` at `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:237-245` appends only `upstream_branch_refs()`.
- `upstream_branch_refs()` at `commit_impact.py:166-193` filtered remote refs with `ref.endswith(f"/{current_local_branch}")`. The fixture repo initializes as local `master` while the test upstream is explicitly `main`, so after a *successful* fetch the scan sees `refs/remotes/origin/main`, returns `[]`, and falls back to `HEAD`-only.

Captured production calls from a throwaway reproduction, which settle that the fetch itself is healthy: `git fetch --quiet` → rc 0, empty stderr; `git symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD` → `master`; `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname) refs/remotes/` → `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` and `refs/remotes/origin/main`; final scan `git log --format=%H%x1f%B%x00 HEAD` → only `init`. A control run with the upstream branch named `master` found the referencing SHA and closed successfully. Not environmental — the local-path fetch needs no credentials.

On age: the test and the close-refresh behaviour were introduced together in `2e81cb9767c1` ("Refresh close commit scan", 2026-09-06), whose parent has neither the test nor `_STALE_REF_MESSAGE`. The fixture already used a plain `git init -q` at that commit, so on any host whose default branch is `master` without an `init.defaultBranch` override it has been broken since introduction. It would only ever have passed where git initializes `main`.

## The fix on this ticket resolves it

Verified directly rather than inferred: the test **passes** in this ticket's worktree at `0885bbf1c31` ("Scan upstream refs minus the tickets branch", Gerrit change 2989), and **fails** at `origin/main`. This ticket's approach — scanning upstream refs while excluding the tickets branch — is strictly broader than the alternative of resolving the remote HEAD target, and it covers the mismatched-branch case that produced the failure.

Practical consequence while 2989 is in review: any `make verify` run from a worktree branched off current `origin/main` will show this one failure. It is this bug, it is already fixed here, and it should not be re-triaged as a regression in the change under test.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`commit_impact.upstream_branch_refs()` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:166-193`)
builds its set of upstream refs by including only refs whose name ends in `/<current-branch>`:

```python
suffix = f"/{name}"
return [ref for ref in listed.stdout.split() if ref.endswith(suffix)]
```

When the local checkout's current branch name differs from the branch the remote commit
lives on, the include-upstream scan silently ignores the correct remote ref — **even after
a successful fetch**.

Discovered incidentally during the sandbox failure census under `rebuffable-pebbly-xenurine`
(`985f-0ec5-a61c-46ee`). It is the one failure in that census with no environmental
component: it reproduces as an ordinary baseline defect.

## Reproduction on baseline main

```
pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -k test_file_impact_close_fetches_before_rejecting_stale_clone
```

fails with:

```
rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar transition failed (exit 1): Error: cannot close
20f8-4f6b-dd8e-486a: it records file_impact (a code change) but no commit references it
(nor any of its descendants).
```

The fixture repo is on the git default branch while the upstream repo is created with
`git init -b main`, so the remote commit lands on `refs/remotes/origin/main`. The gate
fetches successfully, then scans upstream refs, finds nothing whose name ends in the local
branch name, and rejects.

## Why this matters

The completion gate's stale-clone path exists precisely to avoid rejecting a close when the
work *has* landed but the local clone had not yet seen it. `AGENTS.md` documents the remedy
for that state as fetching and fast-forwarding. This defect means the fetch can succeed and
the gate still reject, because the scan is looking under the wrong ref name.

The practical consequence is a false "cannot confirm the work landed" on any checkout whose
branch name does not match the remote branch — a throwaway worktree, a clone left on
`master`, or any branch naming that diverges from the upstream branch. The failure is a
false negative, which is the safe direction, but it blocks legitimate closes and pushes
operators toward overrides.

## Determination: which refs the scan must select

Acceptance criterion 4 of the original report asked for a choice between scanning all
upstream refs, resolving the configured upstream branch, or using the ref the fetch updated.
The choice is **scan every remote-tracking ref except the ticket event-log branch**, for
these reasons, all read out of the current code:

1. `referencing_commits`'s own docstring states the `include_upstream` question as "did this
   ticket ever ship a commit?", and describes the target state as "a checkout that is
   fetched but never checked out ... holds the referencing commit on
   `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` while HEAD still points at the clone-time commit".
   Branch identity is not part of that question.
2. The same docstring gives exactly one reason for not using `--all`: "rebar's default store
   layout keeps the ticket event log on a `tickets` BRANCH OF THE SAME REPOSITORY, so
   `--all` would walk one commit per ticket event — the wrong history, and an unbounded
   amount of it." That reason is served precisely by excluding the configured tickets
   branch, and the local-branch-name filter is a coincidental proxy for it.
3. The gate already accepts a commit that is merely reachable from local HEAD and has not
   landed anywhere. Requiring upstream matches to additionally sit on a same-named branch is
   strictly inconsistent with that, so the selection rule is not carrying a safety property.

Resolving the configured upstream (`@{upstream}`) was rejected: the stale-clone shape in the
failing test has no tracking configuration at all, so `@{upstream}` is unset and the scan
would still find nothing. Using "the ref the fetch updated" was rejected because the fetch
and the scan are separate call sites and threading a ref between them widens the change
without covering a clone that was fetched by some other means.

The tickets branch name comes from `config.tickets_branch()` (`_config_schema.TrackerConfig.branch`,
default `tickets`), which is the accessor every other consumer already uses, so a repo that
renames its event-log branch stays excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `upstream_branch_refs` selects remote-tracking refs by excluding the configured
      ticket event-log branch rather than by matching the local branch name, so the result
      no longer depends on local and remote branch names agreeing.
- [x] A new test fixes the fixture on one branch name and the remote commit on another, and
      asserts the close succeeds; it fails on baseline and passes after the change. Run with
      `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py`.
- [x] `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -k test_file_impact_close_fetches_before_rejecting_stale_clone`
      passes, having been verified failing on baseline `main` first.
- [x] A unit test asserts `upstream_branch_refs` omits `refs/remotes/<remote>/tickets` when
      that ref exists, so the ticket event log is still never walked as code history.
- [x] `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -k test_file_impact_close_distinguishes_refreshed_absence`
      still passes, proving the gate continues to refuse a clone where the work genuinely
      has not landed upstream.
- [x] [non-codebase] The full verify suite is green for this change, with the run and its
      exit code recorded on this ticket. The authoritative signal is the Gerrit `Verified`
      vote on this change's patch set, which runs the same selection `make test` runs.
      provenance: environment=github-actions-hosted-runner; principal=rebar-ci-bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — CI run 35488597727 executed the gating suite against Gerrit change 2989 patch set 1 (revision 0885bbf1c3153908dbd7d1c75a70529e57ad8fa2) and concluded SUCCESS, casting `Verified +1`; that run is the same merge gate that admits the change to `main`, so its exit status is the authoritative verify result rather than a simulation of one.

## Testing

`pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py` covers the close-gate paths:
the differing-branch-name close that currently fails, the genuine-absence refusal that must
keep refusing, and the unrefreshable-clone case. A unit test over `upstream_branch_refs`
asserts the tickets ref is excluded and a differently-named code branch is included.
`make verify` is the pre-push gate and must exit 0.

## Notes

The defect is in ref *selection*, not in the fetch, which succeeds. This is adjacent to
`working-carnelian-bobwhite` (`8806-198c-e2d6-46ce`), which concerns the completion gate
verifying against a stale tree; both are defects in what tree or ref the gate considers
authoritative.

reproduction for the differing-branch-name close, and regression coverage that genuine absence is still refused
unit coverage that upstream_branch_refs excludes the tickets ref and includes a differently-named code branch
